literal.prompt: В каком городе находится Красная площадь?

literalGroups.primaryGround: UNESCO identifies the site by the explicit title “Kremlin and Red Square, Moscow” and places Red Square at the historic/geographic centre of Moscow beneath the east wall of the Kremlin (L2-L5, L46-L48, L60). This supports Moscow as the sole correct city. The four answer labels are all Russian cities; each distractor’s own fact is separately grounded below.

literalGroups.literal: Это Москва. Красная площадь лежит у восточной стены Московского Кремля; на её южном конце стоит собор Василия Блаженного.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The edited two-sentence explanation names Moscow, locates Red Square at the Kremlin’s east wall, and adds the Basilica of St Basil at the square’s south end, exactly as UNESCO states (L47, L60-L63). It avoids the former subjective “one of the most recognizable” claim.

literalGroups.literal: Красная площадь расположена в центре Москвы рядом с Кремлём.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The note says the square is in central Moscow beside the Kremlin. UNESCO identifies the Kremlin as being at Moscow’s geographic and historic centre (L47), and Red Square as lying beneath its east wall (L60), supporting both clauses.

literalGroups.literal: Ярославль — город в России, административный центр Ярославской области.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The official MCHS Yaroslavl regional office identifies Yaroslavl as the administrative centre of Yaroslavl Oblast; its site is explicitly the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations and Yaroslavl region context is shown in the page header. This grounds the own-option note.

literalGroups.literal: Смоленск — город в России, административный центр Смоленской области, Город-герой.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The official Smolensk regional government page states that Smolensk is the administrative, industrial and cultural centre of Smolensk Oblast and has the title “Hero City” (since 6 May 1985), directly supporting the note’s key own-option facts.

literalGroups.literal: Владимир — древний российский город на реке Клязьме.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The official Vladimir municipal history states that Vladimir was founded in 990 or 992 and quotes the Ipatiev Chronicle placing the city by the Klyazma; it further describes the city on the river’s high bank. This supports “ancient city on the Klyazma.”
